newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open little changed amid lack of data.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open little changed amid lack of data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened little changed in quiet trade on Monday, taking their direction from U.S. Treasuries amid a lack of significant economic news or data, analysts said.

"It's pretty uneventful here right now, that's for sure. It's just very, very quiet," said one bond trader with a bank-owned brokerage. "There's no news out today both in the U.S. and here. There's just nothing happening."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.12 to C$117.01 to yield 6.678 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.67 percent. The negative spread between the two bonds was one basis point, unchanged from Friday's close.
Canadian data on international security transactions out this morning had little impact on the bond market, analysts said.

Instead the market is focused largely on a report U.S. durable goods orders out on Wednesday. Beyond that the market is already looking ahead to the meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate-setting Open Market Committee on July 1.
"We've got a few things this week, but I guess if anything we have the Fed meeting the first week of July. I think that's really what we're looking for here," said the trader.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.15 to C$108.46 to yield 6.098 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent which traded unchanged to yield 6.38 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 28 basis points from 30 basis points at Friday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.80 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.08 percent.
